title: Measuring Velocity
description: Define average velocity from a position function and use it to estimate instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocities over shrinking time intervals.
subskills: Compute average velocity over an interval [a,b] using AV = (s(b) - s(a))/(b - a), including units
Interpret average velocity as the slope of a secant line on a position graph
Estimate instantaneous velocity by computing average velocities over progressively smaller intervals
Interpret the sign of velocity as direction of motion and relate it to the slope of the tangent line

title: Limits -- Understanding & Computation
description: Understand limits intuitively from graphs and tables, and evaluate them algebraically using direct substitution, factoring, and rationalizing; connect the limiting process to how average velocity approximates instantaneous velocity.
subskills: Estimate limits from graphs and tables of values
Evaluate limits by direct substitution
Resolve indeterminate forms 0/0 by factoring or rationalizing the numerator or denominator
Connect the limiting process to how average velocity over shrinking time intervals approaches instantaneous velocity (S-1)

title: Derivative at a Point & as a Function
description: Define the derivative -- at a point and as a function -- using the limit of the difference quotient; interpret it as the instantaneous rate of change and slope of the tangent line, and represent it graphically.
subskills: Write and evaluate the limit definition of the derivative at a point and as a function
Interpret f'(a) as the slope of the tangent line and instantaneous rate of change, and distinguish the value f'(a) from the function f'(x)
Estimate derivative values from graphs or tables of values
Sketch the graph of f' from the graph of f and determine where f is differentiable

title: Interpreting, Estimating & Using the Derivative
description: Interpret the meaning and units of the derivative in applied contexts, and estimate derivative values from tabular or graphical data.
subskills: Interpret the meaning of f'(x) in an applied context (population, depreciation, temperature, etc.)
Determine the units of f'(x) as (units of f) per (unit of x)
Estimate f'(x) from tabular data using average rates of change / central differences
Use f'(x) to predict how f will change for a one-unit change in x

title: Higher-Order Derivatives
description: Compute second and higher-order derivatives and interpret their physical and geometric meaning.
subskills: Compute f''(x) and f^(3)(x) using repeated differentiation
Interpret f''(x) as acceleration in motion problems
Determine concavity from the sign of f''(x)
Use Leibniz notation for higher-order derivatives: d2y/dx2

title: Continuity
description: Define continuity at a point and on an interval using one-sided and two-sided limits; classify types of discontinuities and determine where a function is continuous.
subskills: Evaluate one-sided limits and determine whether a two-sided limit exists, including for piecewise functions
State and apply the three conditions for continuity at a point
Identify removable, jump, and infinite discontinuities and determine intervals of continuity for composite and piecewise functions
Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)

title: Tangent Lines & Linear Approximation
description: Write equations of tangent lines to curves at given points and use linearization to approximate function values.
subskills: Find the equation of a tangent line y = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a)
Use the tangent line as a local linear approximation
Compute differentials: dy = f'(x)dx
Estimate function values using linearization

title: Differentiation Rules
description: Apply standard differentiation rules -- power rule, constant rule, sum/difference rule, constant multiple rule -- to differentiate polynomial and rational functions.
subskills: Apply the power rule for integer and rational exponents
Differentiate sums, differences, and constant multiples
Differentiate polynomial functions efficiently
Differentiate rational functions using algebra + power rule

title: Derivatives of Transcendental Functions
description: Differentiate trigonometric and exponential functions.
subskills: Differentiate sin x and cos x
Differentiate tan x and the reciprocal trigonometric functions
Differentiate the natural exponential function e^x
Differentiate exponential functions a^x and use the required factor ln(a)

title: Product & Quotient Rules
description: Differentiate products and quotients of functions using the product rule and quotient rule.
subskills: State and apply the product rule: (fg)' = f'g + fg'
State and apply the quotient rule: (f/g)' = (f'g - fg')/g^2
Differentiate products and quotients involving polynomial and rational functions
Differentiate and simplify products and quotients involving trigonometric and exponential functions

title: Chain Rule
description: Differentiate composite functions using the chain rule, including nested compositions.
subskills: Identify inner and outer functions in a composition
Apply the chain rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x)
Differentiate functions like sin(x^2), e^(3x), (x^2+1)^5
Apply chain rule repeatedly for nested compositions

title: Derivatives of Inverse Functions
description: Differentiate inverse functions -- including logarithms and inverse trigonometric functions -- using the inverse function derivative rule.
subskills: Apply the inverse function derivative rule: if g is the inverse of f, then g'(x) = 1/f'(g(x))
Derive and use derivatives of ln x and log_a x from inverse and change-of-base relationships
Differentiate the inverse trigonometric functions arcsin x, arccos x, and arctan x
Differentiate compositions involving inverse functions using the chain rule (e.g., arctan(3x), ln(x^2+1))

title: Implicit Differentiation
description: Use implicit differentiation to find dy/dx when y is defined implicitly by an equation in x and y.
subskills: Differentiate both sides of an implicit equation with respect to x
Solve for dy/dx after differentiating
Find the slope of a tangent line to an implicit curve at a point
Apply implicit differentiation to relations like x^2 + y^2 = r^2

title: Related Rates
description: Solve related rates problems by differentiating equations relating multiple quantities with respect to time.
subskills: Identify all quantities that change with time
Write an equation relating the quantities
Differentiate implicitly with respect to t
Substitute known values to find the unknown rate

title: L'Hopital's Rule
description: Apply L'Hopital's Rule to evaluate limits of indeterminate forms such as 0/0 and infinity/infinity.
subskills: Identify indeterminate forms: 0/0, inf/inf, 0*inf, inf-inf, 1^inf, 0^0
Apply L'Hopital's Rule correctly (differentiate numerator and denominator separately)
Apply the rule repeatedly when needed
Rewrite indeterminate products and differences before applying the rule

title: Mean Value Theorem
description: State and apply Rolle's Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem (MVT) to analyze function behavior.
subskills: State the hypotheses and conclusion of the MVT
Find values of c satisfying the MVT on a given interval
Apply Rolle's Theorem as a special case of MVT
Use MVT to argue about function behavior (e.g., uniqueness of zeros)

title: Monotonicity, Critical Points & Concavity
description: Use the first and second derivatives to determine where a function is increasing, decreasing, or concave, to classify critical points and extrema, and to sketch curves.
subskills: Find critical numbers and determine intervals where a function is increasing or decreasing
Apply the First and Second Derivative Tests to identify and classify local extrema
Determine concavity and find inflection points where f'' changes sign
Sketch curves using information from f, f', and f''

title: Optimization
description: Model and solve optimization problems by identifying objective functions and constraints, then applying calculus to find absolute extrema.
subskills: Set up an objective function from a word problem
Use constraint equations to reduce to one variable
Find critical points on a closed interval using the Closed Interval Method
Verify that the critical point is a maximum or minimum

title: Riemann Sums & Definite Integrals
description: Define the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums and interpret it geometrically as signed area under a curve.
subskills: Write left, right, and midpoint Riemann sum approximations
Express the definite integral as the limit as n -> infinity of the sum of f(xi*) * delta-x
Interpret the definite integral as net area under a curve
Use basic properties of definite integrals (linearity, interval splitting)

title: Average Value of a Function
description: Compute the average value of a function on an interval using the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals.
subskills: Apply the average value formula: f_avg = (1/(b-a)) times the integral from a to b of f(x) dx
State and apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
Interpret average value in applied contexts (e.g., average temperature, velocity)
Find the value(s) of c where f(c) equals the average value

title: Antiderivatives & the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: Find antiderivatives using basic integration rules, and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives.
subskills: Reverse the power rule and integrate basic trig, exponential, and 1/x functions to find antiderivatives
Write the general antiderivative F(x) + C, and find a particular antiderivative using an initial condition
State the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: the integral from a to b of f(x) dx = F(b) - F(a), where F is any antiderivative of f
Evaluate definite integrals using antiderivatives

title: The Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
description: Construct accumulation functions A(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt and apply the Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to differentiate them, connecting properties of f to properties of A.
subskills: Construct an accumulation function A(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt from a given function f
Apply the Second FTC to differentiate accumulation functions: A'(x) = f(x)
Relate properties of f -- sign, increasing/decreasing, concavity -- to corresponding properties of A
Explain how the Second FTC and evaluation via antiderivatives (S-21) both express the inverse relationship between differentiation and integration

title: u-Substitution
description: Evaluate integrals using the substitution rule (u-substitution) as the integration analog of the chain rule.
subskills: Choose an appropriate substitution u = g(x)
Rewrite the integral entirely in terms of u
Apply substitution to both indefinite and definite integrals
Handle limits of integration correctly when substituting in definite integrals

title: Area Between Curves
description: Use definite integrals to compute the area of regions bounded by two or more curves.
subskills: Find intersection points of two curves
Set up the integral of [f(x) - g(x)] dx for area between curves
Handle cases where curves switch which is on top
Compute area using vertical or horizontal slicing as appropriate
